messages.subject: Backwards compatible version of gbm
messages.body_plain: I've noticed that the CRAN version of gbm has been slightly updated and recently orphaned. Given all the good, but breaking changes in the 2.2 series, is there any objection to keeping a separate backwards compatible version on CRAN? In a similar spirit to lme4.0 perhaps? I wouldn't mind maintaining it, but not if this was already in the works.

messages.subject: RE: Support for left truncated data
messages.body_plain:
Terry Therneau has worked with the gbm-developer team to intergrate his survival code into the latest version of gbm. I’ve not experimented with it extensively.

Use the latest version on github, https://github.com/gbm-developers/gbm.

In your gbm outcome use a Surv() object that captures your particular censoring, like

Surv(t0,t1,event,type="interval2")

Definitely read ?Surv for specific information on how to code the times, events, and the different censoring types.

Greg

From: gbm...@googlegroups.com [mailto:gbm...@googlegroups.com] On Behalf Of Megan Payne
Sent: Monday, March 27, 2017 6:56 AM
To: gbm developers <gbm...@googlegroups.com>
Subject: Support for left truncated data

Hi, I am working on a project where I have left truncated and right censored data from a clinical trial. There could be people who have an event (shortly?) after diagnosis and before entering the clinical trial. I am using gbm to model the data. Up until now, I have been ignoring the left truncation issue because I could not find reference to truncated data in the documentation. Does gbm support truncated data?

--

messages.subject: Re: Support for left truncated data
messages.body_plain:
I added the underlying support for (start, stop] data, which will accomodate left truncation.  The use of interval censored data is not valid and should generate an error, but I have not done much testing of the new code.

Terry T.

On 03/27/2017 08:42 AM, Greg Ridgeway wrote:

> Terry Therneau has worked with the gbm-developer team to intergrate his survival code into the latest version of gbm. I’ve not experimented with it extensively.
>
>
>
> Use the latest version on github, https://github.com/gbm-developers/gbm.
>
>
>
> In your gbm outcome use a Surv() object that captures your particular censoring, like
>
> Surv(t0,t1,event,type="interval2")
>
>
>
> Definitely read ?Surv for specific information on how to code the times, events, and the different censoring types.
>
>
>
> Greg
>
>
>
> From: gbm...@googlegroups.com [mailto:gbm...@googlegroups.com] On Behalf Of Megan Payne
> Sent: Monday, March 27, 2017 6:56 AM
> To: gbm developers <gbm...@googlegroups.com>
> Subject: Support for left truncated data
>
>
>
> Hi, I am working on a project where I have left truncated and right censored data from a clinical trial. There could be people who have an event (shortly?) after diagnosis and before entering the clinical trial. I am using gbm to model the data. Up until now, I have been ignoring the left truncation issue because I could not find reference to truncated data in the documentation. Does gbm support truncated data?
>
